title: Manuel Neuer rules out reversing Germany retirement for the World Cup
content:
Manuel Neuer has ruled out the possibility of coming out of retirement to play for Germany at the 2026 World Cup.

Neuer, 39, ended his international career after the 2024 European Championship, but has remained in excellent form for Bayern Munich in the 18 months since. Marc-Andre ter Stegen, long expected to be his successor internationally, has suffered a series of injuries during that time, prompting suggestions that Neuer — who won the World Cup in 2014 and made 124 appearances for Germany — would reverse his decision.

However, following Bayern’s 2-0 win over RB Leipzig in the DFB-Pokal quarter-final on Wednesday night, Neuer was asked whether his retirement was permanent.

“Yes,” he told Sky Deutschland, before offering support for Hoffenheim’s Oliver Baumann, who is head coach Julian Nagelsmann’s current first choice.

“He’s number one now and he’s doing his job very well. He’s performing very well. And I’m keeping my fingers crossed for him. I wish him all the best.”

Neuer also expressed sympathy for Ter Stegen. The Barcelona goalkeeper is currently on loan at Girona and last week suffered a hamstring tear. In the last two years, the 33-year-old has also suffered a serious back injury and a patella tendon tear, limiting him to just ten appearances in La Liga during that period.

“That’s obviously really tough,” Neuer said, responding to questions about ter Stegen’s most recent injury. “He’ll be back, but it’s obviously really disappointing, especially with the timing and the World Cup coming up this summer.

“He had that as a goal and all we can do is keep our fingers crossed that he comes back and regains his old form.”

The clarity Neuer has provided is really useful. The story of his potential comeback has fascinated parts of the German media for months now and has drawn comment from all parts — ex-player, pundits, fans.

It has been unhelpful. Germany are among the favourites for the World Cup and having disappointed so profoundly at the previous two tournaments — being eliminated in the group stage in 2018 and 2022 — having any sort of uncertainty within this preparation phase was hardly ideal.

In addition to which, it has been unfair to Oliver Baumann. Baumann, the Hoffenheim goalkeeper, is not and has never been Neuer’s equal. Had it not been for Ter Stegen’s injury issues, he likely would never have had the chance to be his country’s starter.

But he has been given that opportunity and has taken it; Baumann has played extremely well in his international appearances this season and deserves to feel secure heading towards the summer — and that includes not have the spectre of Neuer, one of German football’s true icons, hovering in the background.
